summary: WorldEntity duplicate-diagnostic retention is only caller-bounded: createRegistry accepts any finite non-negative safe integer capacity, so a valid configuration can retain an effectively unbounded number of duplicate diagnostics. Define a project-owned maximum and lock exact-limit/one-over behavior after the active generation-4 WorldEntity recovery, rather than broadening PR #378 mid-recovery.
evidence: PR #378 exact head 4680b8176c144b99ffeb1754eb94c03e7bfe42c6: createRegistry defaults to 64 but otherwise validates duplicateDiagnosticCapacity only with assertNonNegativeInteger, whose upper bound is MAX_SAFE_INTEGER = 9007199254740991.
The duplicate path trims only when #duplicates >= capacity, then inserts the new frozen diagnostic; therefore retained history scales directly with the caller-provided capacity.

Current PR #378 tests exercise registry/state hardening but do not expose a project-owned MAX_DUPLICATE_DIAGNOSTIC_CAPACITY or exact-limit/one-over capacity regression; the legacy suite only rejects invalid/non-finite capacity.

Repository PR search found the original #58 claim that duplicate history stays explicitly bounded and #276 malformed-capacity tests, but no follow-on lane or PR establishing a hard maximum for a valid capacity value.
UNRENDERED quality canon requires caches, queues, and budgets to be bounded and observable; accepting a max-safe-integer diagnostic retention budget leaves this cache boundary effectively unbounded.

metadata.recommendedClosure: Add an explicit documented maximum diagnostic capacity, reject one-over before allocation/retention, preserve default 64 and zero-capacity semantics, and add exact-limit/one-over pure regressions. Schedule after the active WorldEntity recovery to avoid overlapping source ownership.
